hypotheses.binder: (hX : Algebra.Smooth K (Localization.Away (weightedSplitTraceLaurentPartialX alpha beta d e)))
hypotheses.justification: The same file proves this unconditionally, for every alpha, beta, d, e: `weightedSplitTracePartialXLocalization_smooth alpha beta d e : Algebra.Smooth K (WeightedSplitTracePartialXLocalization alpha beta d e)` (line 236). That lemma needs no hypotheses because the chart has a submersive presentation whose Jacobian is a unit after localization. `WeightedSplitTracePartialXLocalization` is an `abbrev` for `Localization.Away (weightedSplitTraceLaurentPartialX alpha beta d e)` (line 140), so its type is the type of hX. To delete hX, add `have hX := weightedSplitTracePartialXLocalization_smooth alpha beta d e` at the start of the proof; nothing else changes. The downstream theorem `weightedSplitTraceLaurent_smooth` already passes exactly this lemma for hX. hX and hY can each be deleted on their own, and also both together.

hypotheses.binder: (hY : Algebra.Smooth K (Localization.Away (weightedSplitTraceLaurentPartialY alpha beta d e)))
hypotheses.justification: The same file proves this unconditionally, for every alpha, beta, d, e: `weightedSplitTracePartialYLocalization_smooth alpha beta d e : Algebra.Smooth K (WeightedSplitTracePartialYLocalization alpha beta d e)` (line 377). It has no hypotheses on the parameters and is proved through a submersive presentation. `WeightedSplitTracePartialYLocalization` is an `abbrev` for `Localization.Away (weightedSplitTraceLaurentPartialY alpha beta d e)` (line 290), so its type is the type of hY. To delete hY, add `have hY := weightedSplitTracePartialYLocalization_smooth alpha beta d e` at the start of the proof; the rest of the proof is unchanged. hspan, by contrast, depends on nondegeneracy conditions on alpha, beta, d, e and the characteristic of K, so it cannot be removed. hY can be deleted on its own, and also together with hX.
